nodes.label: Customer screens
nodes.rationale:
The anonymous customer home page offers **Create account** alongside sign-in. Registration collects name, email, optional phone and a password of 15–128 Unicode code points, and sends the current language preference. Pending-account feedback explains email confirmation, spam folders and resend limits without revealing whether an account already exists. Request failures allow deliberate retry; passwords are cleared after each settled attempt and are never persisted. Closing the dialog aborts its request. Keyboard focus, Escape, labeled inputs and pending controls use the shared accessible dialog components.

Email links open `/auth/action` with their purpose and token in the fragment. The page immediately removes the fragment and query from browser history and retains the token only in memory. Opening a link does not confirm the account: the customer must press **Confirm email**. Same-page replacement links abort prior requests and reset the screen. Invalid, expired, replaced or used links offer resend; transient failures permit retry. Refreshing the cleaned URL requires a new email link. Confirmation creates no session; the customer returns home to sign in separately. I14 shares this landing page with password recovery/reset; initial setup and relationship purposes remain unavailable until their owning tasks implement them.

Production frontend hosting must serve the SPA for `/auth/action`. Keep third-party analytics and content off this secret-bearing landing page. The existing explicitly invoked delivery worker must run to deliver pending email; these screens do not install a production scheduler or provider.

Verification is recorded in [Identity evidence](../tasks/identity-verification.md), including real Spanish/English Mailpit delivery, resend, revoked and used links, keyboard navigation, accessible errors and responsive layouts. The user approved I12. I13/I14 now provide the recovery backend and shared recovery screens.

Primary references: [node-postgres transactions](https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions) and [OWASP authentication responses](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html).

UI references: [React StrictMode](https://react.dev/reference/react/StrictMode) and [History.replaceState](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/History/replaceState).

nodes.label: I13 - password recovery backend
nodes.description:
The user approved the I12 human-review checkpoint and authorized I13 on October 3, 2026. The [recovery guide](../docs/identity-recovery.md) defines request/reset POST contracts, exact Origin and anonymous CSRF, eligibility and generic acceptance, one-hour purpose-bound single-use links, resend limits and all-session revocation. Recovery preserves account status, roles and confirmation provenance. Existing registration/confirmation and recovery share the extracted durable public-action limit; request budgets remain distinct while reset shares confirmation's action-IP budget.

Implementation was delivered in small service/test, route/composition and documentation slices. Initial tests failed on the absent recovery module and routes. Test fixtures then exposed existing confirmation-exemption provenance and deactivation timestamp constraints; corrected fixtures supply their required provenance/timestamps without weakening those constraints. Five focused real PostgreSQL scenarios passed before broader regression, covering actual HTTP Origin/CSRF/GET/body denial, single-use concurrent reset, old-credential and all-session denial, exempt-account recovery, generic request replies, resend replacement/limits, exact one-hour expiry, inactive people/accounts, stale versions, wrong-purpose links, input/mass-assignment rejection, and atomic rollback when audit writing fails. A sixth scenario adds local fixture success, copied fixture denial under production environment and durable reset-IP limits across service instances.

Independent read-only review found no Critical or Required defects in recovery eligibility, locks, session revocation, audit rollback, routes or the shared limiter. Its optional copied-fixture test was added; simultaneous login/reset remains covered by the existing account-lock/version guards and inspection, without a new dedicated race test. Runtime evidence for real inbox delivery and frontend reset is reserved for I14; existing action delivery and browser regressions still apply. Production timing uniformity is not claimed.
